title: Dotlineform Projects Report Customisation Decision Delivery
summary: assess the recreated dotlineform projects collection against the default report and decide whether a Projects customisation is justified
content_html:
Dotlineform Projects Report Customisation Decision Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as SSR-3, after SSR-2 has recreated dotlineform/projects through the real lifecycle and populated it with representative documents.

This is an evidence-led product and architecture decision. It does not assume that Projects is a Tags-style preset or that every sub-scope requires a custom module.

Complete Outcome

The working Projects collection is reviewed against the shipped default. The delivery records one of two accepted outcomes:

  1. the default is sufficient, with no Projects customisation identity; or
  2. Projects has specific justified needs, expressed as a bounded customisation contract and separate implementation delivery.

The decision identifies the actual user tasks, data required, controls or presentation involved, exact targets, capability gates, and public/Manage boundary. It does not leave a vague list of desirable report features.

Assessment Questions

  • Which Projects tasks are not adequately served by title search, list/detail navigation, New, and app-level Import?
  • Which document fields are stable collection data rather than body content or temporary workflow state?
  • Is last_updated useful for visible recency, sorting, or filtering in this collection, and should that use remain Projects-specific or revise the default?
  • Does Projects need filtering, sorting, grouping, row metadata, selection, a package workflow, or validated-detail actions?
  • Is each proposed action collection-, checked-selection-, or validated-document-targeted?
  • Can a generic helper already provided by the framework satisfy the need, or is Projects-specific presentation/behaviour required?
  • Does any public Projects view need the same customisation, or is the need Manage-only?

Decision Method

[ ] SSR-3.0 — Representative Use

  • [ ] Populate the recreated collection with enough real Projects documents to expose meaningful differences in status, dates, metadata, and workflow.
  • [ ] Use the default report for ordinary discovery, opening, creation, editing, and Import.
  • [ ] Record concrete failed or awkward tasks without treating preference or anticipated scale as a requirement.

Checkpoint: review evidence names real documents and tasks while preserving their exact collection identity. Stop before proposing controls.

[ ] SSR-3.1 — Customisation Options

  • [ ] Map each evidenced need to default behaviour, a reusable optional helper, a Projects-owned contribution, or a non-report workflow.
  • [ ] Reject additions that duplicate title search, app-level Import, source editing, or another established owner.
  • [ ] For each retained addition, define its data source, placement, target, capability, empty state, refresh effect, and public/Manage access.
  • [ ] Review representative dense, empty, and narrow-screen states where the decision depends on presentation.

Checkpoint: every proposed Projects difference has an owner and measurable outcome; none relies on a Projects conditional in the default engine.

[ ] SSR-3.2 — Accept Default Or Create Delivery

  • [ ] If the default is sufficient, record that result and leave Projects customisation unset.
  • [ ] If customisation is justified, freeze one registered Projects identity and create a separate bounded implementation delivery under the feature parent.
  • [ ] Revisit the default only when evidence shows the behaviour is appropriate for an ordinary new collection, not merely useful to Projects.
  • [ ] Update the feature parent and stop for review.

Fixed Boundaries

  • No Projects behaviour is inferred from Analysis/Tags groups or actions.
  • No implementation begins inside this decision delivery beyond disposable review fixtures or explicitly approved diagnostic prototypes.
  • The report manifest remains data, not executable action configuration.
  • The decision cannot weaken exact-target, capability, public-isolation, or app-level Import contracts.
  • A Projects need owned by another surface becomes a separate feature or delivery rather than widening docs_subscope.

Completion Gates

  • The decision is based on the recreated working collection, not hypothetical parity with Tags.
  • Every accepted difference has a concrete task, owner, data contract, target, and access boundary.
  • The outcome explicitly says either default sufficient or links one new implementation delivery.
  • Projects remains comparable to other sub-scopes through the standard customisation framework, without becoming a new report type.
